descriptionChirho: The sense of pais as 'servant' or 'slave,' denoting one who serves a master or, in theological usage, a servant of God. Includes the centurion's servant (Matt 8:6, 8, 13 'my servant is lying paralyzed'), Jesus as the Servant of God in Isaianic fulfillment quotations (Matt 12:18 'my servant whom I have chosen'; Acts 3:13, 26; 4:25, 27, 30 'your holy servant Jesus'), David as God's servant (Luke 1:69; Acts 4:25), Israel as God's servant (Luke 1:54), and the plural 'servants' (Matt 14:2 Herod's servants, Luke 12:45 menservants, Luke 15:26 servants in the Prodigal Son). Hebrew 'eved/avadīm ('servant/slaves'), Arabic 'abd, Korean jong ('servant'), Spanish siervo. This usage draws on the LXX tradition of pais as a translation for Hebrew 'eved, particularly in the Servant Songs of Isaiah.

The sense of pais as 'child,' 'boy,' or 'girl,' denoting a young person irrespective of servile status. Includes the children slaughtered by Herod (Matt 2:16), children crying in the temple (Matt 21:15), the epileptic boy healed by Jesus (Matt 17:18), Jairus' daughter (Luke 8:51, 54 'the child'), the child Jesus presented in the temple (Luke 9:42), the royal official's son (John 4:51 'your child lives'), the young man Eutychus (Acts 20:12 'the boy'), and the boy Jesus at age twelve (Luke 2:43). Hebrew na'ar/na'arāh/yeladīm ('boy/girl/children'), Arabic ghulām, Korean ai/sonyeon ('child/boy'), Spanish niño/muchacho. Distinguished from the 'servant' sense by the Hebrew mapping to na'ar rather than 'eved and by the contextual focus on age and youth rather than social role or servile status.
